body: Recent speech LLMs can leverage rich paralinguistic cues, enabling more complex and personalized interactions. However, little work investigates how this sensitivity can lead to stereotyping, and existing evaluations largely measure demographic disparities without distinguishing beneficial personalization from stereotypical behavior. We introduce BASIS-Bench, a benchmark designed to disentangle these two aspects through three axes: (1) demographic robustness, measuring disparities in content-based tasks across speakers and demographic classification capabilities; (2) stereotypical bias, measuring whether perceived demographic cues trigger unprompted stereotypical behavior; and (3) personalization, measuring whether models can tailor responses to demographic characteristics when explicitly requested. We evaluate eight recent speech LLMs and find that, despite often recognizing demographic cues, most fail to translate them into appropriate personalization. Explicit demographic labels improve personalization but also amplify stereotypical associations already present in the textual backbones. These findings highlight the need to train speech LLMs not only to perceive demographic cues, but to learn when they should shape their responses.
summaryZh: 该研究引入了BASIS-Bench基准，旨在评估语音大模型在处理人口统计学线索时的表现。研究发现，尽管模型能识别这些线索，但往往难以将其转化为适当的个性化响应，反而容易放大文本骨干模型中已有的刻板印象。该基准通过人口统计鲁棒性、刻板印象偏见和个性化三个维度进行评估，为提升语音交互的公平性提供了评估框架。
